name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Adrian Smith running with large cash advantage
model.rationale: The R+27 district, Smith's incumbency and roughly 30-to-1 fundraising edge over Becky Stille leave no credible path for a Democratic upset, and prediction markets agree at about 96% Republican. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only realistic route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nebraska's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Adrian Smith, the longtime incumbent, is running for another term and holds a decisive financial advantage: he has raised about $1.8 million with over $1 million on hand, while Democrat Becky Stille has raised roughly $55,000 and has minimal cash. No outside groups are opposing Smith, and no independent or third-party candidates show meaningful funding.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets price Smith's chances at about 96%. With the incumbent, the district lean, and the money gap all aligned, this race is rated Safe Republican, with only a small chance of an upset.
